In the present study, Mg-6Zn-1Zr (ZK60) alloy with a homogeneous fine-grained structure (~5 µm) was produced by hot extrusion.
The material used in this study was as-extruded ZK60 (Mg–5.50Zn–0.55Zr, in wt%) Mg alloy sheet with 40 mm width and 5 mm thickness (extrusion ratio R=26) followed by homogenization at 320 °C for 3 h.

For convenience, samples with tension directions along the extrusion direction, transverse direction and 45° rotated from ED of the as-extruded ZK60 alloy were labeled as ED-, TD- and 45D sample, respectively.
The ED sample has a high yield strength of ~203 MPa, moderate ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of ~314 MPa and a relatively low elongation (εf) of ~15%.

For convenience, samples with tension directions along the extrusion direction, transverse direction and 45° rotated from ED of the as-extruded ZK60 alloy were labeled as ED-, TD- and 45D sample, respectively.
The TD sample, however, exhibits moderate yield strength of ~147 MPa, while a higher UTS of ~327 MPa and higher elongation of ~36%.

At ambient temperature, plastic deformation of magnesium is limited mainly to basal {0001} < 1120 > slip and {1012} < 1011> mechanical twinning
Prismatic <a> slip and {1011} contraction twinning are considered to be hard deformation mechanisms, leading to a high yield stress and low fracture elongation

The CRSS of the prismatic <a> slip is far less than that of the {1011} contraction twinning, so the yielding should be predominated by the prismatic <a> slip, while {1011} contraction twinning operates as the flow stress further increases.
In contrast, in addition to the hard deformation of prismatic <a> slip and {1011} contraction twinning, the {1012} extension twinning can be easily activated by tensile stress along the c-axis

The high superplasticity together with the well-maintained fine grain structure suggests that GBS could occur and should play an important role in the as-extruded ZK60 alloy during tensile testing at 275 °C under a strain rate of 10−3 s−1.
